minutes.headline: Committee approved school calendar changes adding teacher prep days for live streaming, despite parent objections to short notice.
minutes.summary: The committee heard a behavioral health update, public comment largely opposed to short-notice live streaming, and the superintendent's explanation of calendar changes tied to a new state live-instruction rule and a union agreement. It approved the calendar changes, the remote MOA, line item transfers, handing the staffing plan to the town manager, twelve policies on third read, and a hockey co-op request. The business manager gave a quarterly budget update and the FY22 identified needs were presented.

what_happened.line: The School Committee approved the school calendar changes 5-0 by roll call, adding teacher prep days tied to a new state live-instruction rule.
Parents in public comment objected to the short notice of live streaming and its burden on teachers, students and working families.
The committee approved the revised LEA remote MOA 5-0 by roll call.
The committee authorized the superintendent to present the five-year staffing plan to the town manager; funding sources for its positions are not yet set.
The business manager reported the FY21 budget on target, with the COVID relief grant ending December 30th and local funds to cover substitutes and a final PPE purchase.

why_it_matters: The calendar change alters the school schedule families plan around, and it was decided on short notice over objections from parents.
Once the COVID relief grant ends, substitute, PPE and food service shortfalls fall on the local school budget, which is funded mostly by taxes.
The five-year staffing plan names positions and costs but no funding source, so it feeds the town's long-range forecast and later budget votes.
